description:
FILED s448n (Opus round-6 agent N), from the #543 probes.  PRE-EXISTING and
visible on the UNTOUCHED "<&" mode.

REPRODUCER (file holds "aaa\nbbb\nccc\n"):

    open(my $s, '<', $f) or die;
    my $first = <$s>;                 # "aaa\n"
    open(my $d, '<&', $s) or die;
    my $next = <$d>;

        perl  src-first=[aaa\n] dup-next=[bbb\n]
        PCL   src-first=[aaa\n] dup-next=[<undef>]

Same divergence with '+<&' (that is where it was found -- the #543 probe
matrix, "shared-pos" row).

CAUSE: the source's SBCL fd-stream has read the whole file into its buffer, so
the OS file offset is already at EOF when %p-open-dup calls sb-posix:dup.  Perl
flushes the source's PerlIO layer before duping, and flushing a READ handle
lseeks the fd back to the logically-consumed position.  PCL already KNOWS that
position -- `tell($s)` answers 4, correctly -- so the fix is to seek the fd to
the stream's logical position before the dup (and, for the "=" fdopen forms,
before handing the fd over).

WHERE: %p-open-dup, beside %p-fd-of-stream (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp).  Note the
symmetric case: an OUTPUT source must be FLUSHED before the dup, or the dup and
the source race on the same offset (that is #542's neighbourhood, but a
different mechanism -- do not merge them without probing both).

BAR: the reproducer for "<&", "+<&" and "<&=" (the fdopen form shares the fd,
so it needs the same seek), plus a write-side probe that shows the fix does not
reorder output; a guard row in Pl/t/print-fh-magic-01.t.

subject: A dup-open does not sync the SOURCE handle's buffered read position to the fd, so the dup starts at EOF where perl continues at the next line
